title: SQL
summary: Queries, indexes and transactions: what every interview asks.
why: ORMs and AI can write queries you never read. Knowing joins, indexes and isolation levels is how you notice the one that scans a million rows or loses an update.

cards.question: What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN?
cards.answer: INNER JOIN returns only rows matching in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all left rows, with NULL in right-side columns when there is no match.

cards.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
cards.answer: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY, so it can use aggregates like COUNT().

cards.question: What is an index and what does it cost?
cards.answer: A structure (usually a B-tree) that speeds up lookups and sorting. It costs space and slows writes, since every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE must maintain it.

cards.question: Does column order matter in a composite index?
cards.answer: Yes. An index (a, b) serves filters on a, or on a and b, but not efficiently on b alone (leftmost prefix rule). Put equality and more selective columns first.

cards.question: Which anomalies do isolation levels prevent?
cards.answer: Read Committed prevents dirty reads; Repeatable Read also prevents non-repeatable reads; Serializable also prevents phantoms and behaves as if transactions ran serially. More isolation, less concurrency.

cards.question: What do window functions offer over GROUP BY?
cards.answer: They compute over a set of related rows without collapsing them: for example ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) to get each user's latest record.
